Subject: Re: Redwood demo — guests can’t ‘Accept’ calendar invite

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the logs. Short answer: we likely hit a GSuite organizer-affinity edge where the original invite was authored by a service account that didn’t propagate per-guest permissions. That makes guest RSVP UX flaky for some external addresses.

Immediate plan (short-term workaround):
1) I’ll generate a temporary Zoom meeting for the demo and paste the join link into the event description and top of the invite. This avoids the accept flow entirely for guests.
2) Camila will re-send a cleaned-up invite authored from my mailbox (mateo@redwood.com) so organizer shows as a Redwood individual instead of the service account.
3) Ben — can your team confirm whether the Redwood Calendar integration will reissue a fresh ICS without stripping attendees? If not, we’ll send an explicit calendar attachment (ICS) and the Zoom link.

I’m working on the Zoom link now and will attach the Redwood one-pager and a meeting ICS. If we need to nudge HarborTech IT to allow contractor accounts, let me know and we’ll provide the event headers for their admin to whitelist.

Proposed fallback event: 2026-09-16 10:00 PT (same slot).

Thanks — Mateo

Looping in a quick ops note — Mateo, Camila:

- Our Calendar integration has a known behavior where invites authored by the integration service account sometimes set the organizer to a canonical alias, which triggers certain GSuite rules for external attendee RSVP suppression. There isn’t a one-click fix for historical invites; best is to reissue from a user mailbox.
- I’ll regenerate the ICS from our user-authoring flow (Ben) and attach here. That file preserves attendees. If that still fails, the Zoom fallback (link below) is the reliable path.

Temporary Zoom meeting (created): https://zoom.us/j/999888777
Passcode: 7421

Action items:
- Mateo: paste Zoom link at the very top of the invite description and add the ICS as an attachment in the next invite.
- Camila: send the updated invite from mateo@redwood.com and include the HarborTech IT contact in CC so their admin sees the headers.
- Alex: if any contractors still can’t join, reply-all with one example email and we’ll provide the organizer headers for IT to inspect.

I attached the regenerated ICS (redwood-demo-temp.ics) in case you want to preview before resending.

Thanks — Ben
